chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Aban from Abd al-Rahman said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about three partners, one of whom made a claim and the other two testified, and he said, 'It is valid.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one partner claims a right and the other two testify in support?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on evidences, this hadith clarifies the admissibility of testimony in commercial partnerships. It establishes that a single claimant’s assertion, corroborated by the testimony of the two other partners, is legally sufficient (yajuz), reflecting the Shia juristic principle that partnership agreements often rely on mutual acknowledgment and witness testimony to resolve disputes without requiring additional proof.
